title: Hyderabadi Chicken Dum Biryani
tagline: The famous kacchi-style biryani — raw marinated chicken cooked under a seal of parboiled rice.
intro: Hyderabadi dum biryani is a royal dish from the kitchens of the Nizams. In the authentic kacchi method, raw marinated chicken is layered directly under partly cooked rice and everything finishes together under a sealed lid, so the meat's juices perfume the rice from below. The result is deeply aromatic and famously elegant.

items: 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cloves, 4 cardamom, 1 bay leaf, 1 tsp caraway (shahi zeera)
½ tsp saffron in 4 tbsp warm milk

method: Mix all marinade ingredients with the chicken and marinate for at least 1 hour (ideally 3).
Rinse and soak the rice 30 minutes; drain.
Spread the marinated chicken in a heavy pot in an even layer.
Boil the water with salt and whole spices, parboil the rice to just 50–60% (very firm), and drain.
Layer the parboiled rice directly over the raw chicken. Top with saffron milk, fried onions, ghee, kewra water, mint and coriander.
Seal the pot tightly (foil then lid, or a dough seal). Cook on high for 3–4 minutes to build steam, then on the lowest heat for 35–40 minutes.
Turn off the heat and rest, sealed, for 10 minutes.
Open and fold very gently, lifting from the bottom so the chicken comes up through the rice.
tips: Because the chicken is raw at layering, the rice must be under-parboiled (50–60%) so both finish together.
Do not open the lid during dum — the trapped steam does the cooking.
A tawa under the pot protects against scorching during the long dum.
toServe: Traditionally paired with mirchi ka salan and burhani raita.
